audit.why: diff EVEN with a 4/10 rating, green tone and 'Favoured matchup' text is internally consistent enough at 48.19% over 166 games, and the mirror changed only the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every row in both layers reads Ryze, including Levels 2 and 3 — where whys[1] and whys[2] and spikes[0] all say Maokai wins the window outright — and Level 6, where whys[4] says neither side has a decisive edge.
audit.why: A chart that says Ryze wins seven rows straight over a 48.19% lane is not describing this matchup, and it contradicts three of its own captions.
audit.corrected: phases[1]/win[1] and phases[2]/win[2] Ryze -> Maokai with ratings 7/10 -> 3/10, phases[4]/win[4] Ryze -> Skill with rating 8/10 -> 5/10. One atomic group, matching the packet and the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is treated as a plain point-and-click root. Riot's text: Maokai becomes UNTARGETABLE and dashes, rooting on arrival — the page never says so, so it never tells you the burst you fire into the dash is wasted. late also spells it 'Twisted Advanced'. No cooldowns anywhere on his kit.
audit.why: Untargetability changes the commit rule from 'root him back' to 'hold everything until he lands'. The dash is 14 seconds at rank 1, Bramble Smash 7, Nature's Grasp 130 — those are the counting windows.
audit.corrected: Untargetable stated in whys[1], spikes[0] and wants.foe[0]; the 14-second dash written into mid; Nature's Grasp added as a retreat-cutter you hold Flash for, since Ryze has no dash.

edits.before: Twisted Advance roots you before your empowered Q fires — he chains W into Q knockback while your only answer is still on cooldown, and he wins that window cleanly.
edits.after: Twisted Advance goes untargetable mid-dash and roots on arrival, so burst fired at it hits nothing and Bramble Smash follows — a 14-second window he wins cleanly.

edits.before: Maokai's Twisted Advance roots you in place before you can proc an empowered Q — he wins every trade in this window if you let him walk up.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is untargetable while it travels and roots on landing — a rotation spent into the dash is wasted, so hold everything until he arrives.

edits.before: Land Twisted Advance to cancel your empowered Q window and chain it into Q knockback before you can reset
edits.after: Dash in untargetable on Twisted Advance, root on arrival, and chain Bramble Smash before you can reset

edits.before: Once you hit levels 4-5 the lane stabilises in your favour: Maokai is immobile enough that you can stand at the edge of E-bounce range, Flux-stack the wave and him simultaneously, and he has no reliable way to punish you for it without blowing Twisted Advance. Track his W cooldown as your primary engage signal — the moment it goes down, walk up, E-Q-W, and walk out under Phase Rush. At level 6, Realm Warp does not give you a combat steroid so do not force the all-in, but it does open a flank threat that forces Maokai off the wave if your team is anywhere near mid.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stabilise in your favour: he is immobile enough that you can sit at the edge of Flux-bounce range, mark him through the wave, and he cannot punish it without spending Twisted Advance — 14 seconds at rank 1, and the only engage he owns. Count it and step up the moment it is gone: Flux, root, empowered Overload, out on Phase Rush. At 6 Realm Warp is no combat steroid, so do not force the all-in; it does open a flank that pulls him off the wave. Nature's Grasp also cuts retreats, so keep Flash for the wall rather than the damage.

edits.before: Your mana-item spike is where this matchup genuinely flips: with Seraph's Embrace online your combo loops fast enough that Maokai cannot out-sustain the repeated Flux cascades even with his passive. In teamfights, Realm Warp is the answer to his tankiness — you blink your damage-dealers past or around him rather than burning spells into his face. He does not scale into a solo-carry threat the way a hard scaler like Nasus does, so you keep the edge; just avoid getting Twisted Advanced out of position and dumped on by his team before your warp channels.
edits.after: Your mana-item spike is where this matchup genuinely flips: with Seraph's Embrace online your combo loops fast enough that Maokai cannot out-sustain the repeated Flux cascades, though Sap Magic makes Grievous Wounds worth the slot. In teamfights, Realm Warp answers his tankiness — you move your damage past him rather than burning spells into his face. He never becomes a solo-carry threat, so you keep the edge; just do not get caught by Twisted Advance out of position and dumped on before the portal channels.

notes: The chart said Ryze wins all seven rows in a 48.19% matchup while three of its own captions described Maokai windows — flipped Levels 2, 3 and 6 as one matched group per the packet and mirror. Mechanically the page missed that Twisted Advance is UNTARGETABLE during the dash, which is the difference between 'root him back' and 'hold everything until he lands'. 'Twisted Advanced' in late is corrected. Left unstated whether his saplings body-block Overload as a first-target projectile — the mirror flagged that as unverified and I did not assert it either.
